resources.string: That is this app\'s own connection; ending it would cut the screen off from the server.
This panel needs the %1$s permission, which this account does not have. Ask whoever runs the server to grant it.
Ending the session also rolls back its open transaction and closes its connection. Use this when ending the statement is not enough.
This server has no availability group (or none this login can see), so there is nothing to report.
Seeing the other servers of a replication setup needs superuser or the pg_read_all_stats (pg_monitor) role. This says nothing about whether the server replicates.
Availability-group state needs the VIEW SERVER STATE permission. This says nothing about whether the server is in a group.

PostgreSQL keeps statement statistics only through the pg_stat_statements extension. A database administrator has to add it to shared_preload_libraries (a restart) and run CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements in this database. The app never changes the server.
The extension exists in this database, but the server was not started with it in shared_preload_libraries, so it records nothing. Add it there and restart the server.
This needs the VIEW SERVER STATE permission.
Normalised statements. Tap one to open it in the editor; nothing is run. Each $1, $2 … becomes :p1, :p2 … and the editor asks for the values when you run it. The copy icon copies the text as it is.
Pulse reads the server\'s counters, which needs the %1$s permission. This account does not have it.
